title: Golden GPU image: driver / CUDA / NCCL compatibility matrix (working notes)

body:
Context / why this doc exists
- We keep getting bitten by “it boots but doesn’t validate” failures during fleet bring-up. Most common causes:
  - driver/CUDA minor mismatch between image + runtime containers
  - NCCL incompatibility (often showing up as all-reduce hang or extreme perf regression)
  - EFA/libfabric/OFI edge cases on AWS (p4d/p5)
  - silent drift when we bump image packages without bumping validation thresholds
- This is a scratchpad, not the canonical standard. Canonical docs live in Confluence under Golden Image Build + Node Baseline; this is the working “what combinations did we actually test” table.

Assumptions (current sprint)
- Primary rollout target: Dedicated bring-up in us-east for A100 first (p4d.24xlarge style), then expand.
- We need at least one “known good stable” channel, and one “candidate” channel we can promote/rollback.
- The validation agent + NCCL smoke test should reflect *real* runtime container behavior (i.e., if runtime uses CUDA 12.2 base, we should validate with CUDA 12.2 userspace too).

Definitions
- Driver = NVIDIA kernel driver version installed on host (e.g., 535.161.07).
- CUDA userspace = the CUDA toolkit/runtime used by validation containers (and often by serving runtime container).
- NCCL = userspace library. We typically install via container or apt packages inside validation image.
- EFA/OFI = AWS networking stack for high-perf collectives. Most NCCL issues we’ve seen are EFA-adjacent.

Quick take / current proposal (as of 2025-10-18)
- Pin CUDA minor for the sprint (avoid “CUDA 12.4 everywhere” until we get stable perf + no hangs in NCCL smoke test).
- Recommended stable lane:
  - A100 (p4d) stable: Driver 535 + CUDA 12.2 userspace + NCCL 2.18.x
- Candidate lane to evaluate:
  - A100 candidate: Driver 550 + CUDA 12.4 + NCCL 2.19+ (ONLY after we resolve EFA hang + canary perf thresholds)

Compatibility matrix (what we tested)

Legend
- ✅ = passed validation (GPU health + kube join + NCCL smoke + perf canary within threshold)
- ⚠️ = passed but with caveats (flakes, perf drop, needs tuning)
- ❌ = failed (repeatable failure / blocked)

Table 1: A100 (AWS p4d / EFA)
- Host OS baseline: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (kernel 5.15.*), containerd, kubelet per baseline

Driver | CUDA userspace used in validation container | NCCL (container) | Result | Notes
- 535.161.07 | 12.2 | 2.18.5 | ✅ | Most reliable combo so far. NCCL all-reduce 256MB completes. Perf canary within ~5% of baseline.
- 535.161.07 | 12.4 | 2.19.3 | ⚠️ | Generally works, but saw ~8–12% variance in all-reduce time depending on EFA driver revision; needs more runs.
- 550.54.14 | 12.2 | 2.18.5 | ⚠️ | Works, but we saw higher flake rate in NCCL smoke test under node churn (suspect timeouts + initial fabric bring-up). Might be OK with increased timeout/backoff.
- 550.54.14 | 12.4 | 2.19.3 | ❌ | Repeatable hang observed in NCCL all-reduce on 2/6 nodes during warm start. Logs show no explicit error; suspect OFI/EFA interaction. Do not use for sprint stable.

Observed error signatures (A100)
- “Hang” mode:
  - Symptom: validation step ‘nccl_smoke’ hits timeout; node remains in Validating.
  - Agent logs: NCCL test launched; no progress after initial rank init.
  - nvidia-smi shows GPUs OK; EFA appears up.
  - Workaround that sometimes helps: reboot node; if repeats, reimage; if still repeats, quarantine.
- “Hard fail” mode:
  - Symptom: nccl-tests exits non-zero, sometimes OFI error.
  - Example snippets we saw (paraphrased):
    - “NCCL WARN NET/OFI plugin: call to fi_getinfo failed”
    - “libfabric error: Provider efa not found / permission issue”

Table 2: H100 (AWS p5 / EFA)
- NOTE: limited H100 coverage this sprint; mostly sanity checks.

Driver | CUDA userspace | NCCL | Result | Notes
- 535.161.07 | 12.2 | 2.18.5 | ⚠️ | Boots and passes GPU health. NCCL smoke passed in small sample, but perf canary thresholds need separate baseline (H100 faster; existing A100 thresholds not applicable).
- 550.54.14 | 12.4 | 2.19.3 | ⚠️ | Mixed results; 1 flake in 5 runs (timeout). Not enough data to call it stable. Keep as candidate-only.

Table 3: L40S (non-EFA / typical PCIe networking)
- We run fewer collectives issues here; NCCL smoke is mostly “does it run” rather than “is fabric perfect.”

Driver | CUDA userspace | NCCL | Result | Notes
- 535.161.07 | 12.2 | 2.18.5 | ✅ | Stable.
- 550.54.14 | 12.4 | 2.19.3 | ✅ | Looks fine so far. Still want to validate inference perf/regression separately.

What we think is happening (hypotheses)
- The “driver 550 + CUDA 12.4 + NCCL 2.19 + EFA” stack is sensitive to startup ordering / timeouts.
- Some failures appear only under provisioning churn (kubelet join + daemonsets starting + validations running). When we run the same NCCL test manually after 10–15 minutes of idle, it’s more likely to pass.
- This suggests we may need:
  - explicit wait-for-network-ready gate before starting NCCL validation
  - increased initial delay + exponential backoff for nccl_smoke
  - stronger signal collection (capture OFI plugin logs, EFA health) when it times out

Actions we already took / in-flight
- Increased timeouts + retries in validation agent (see github://redwood/pr-18481).
- Adjusted step ordering proposal: GPU health + driver parity -> kube join -> network throughput -> NCCL smoke -> perf canary.
- Started tracking flake rate by image channel + region (hooking into dashboards).

Upgrade plan proposal (candidate -> stable)
1) Stable channel policy (for sprint)
   - Only promote a driver/CUDA/NCCL combo to stable if:
     - nccl_smoke pass rate >= 99.5% over rolling 24h in the staged region/pool
     - time-to-ready P95 does not regress > 10% vs prior stable
     - no new high-sev incidents tied to provisioning/validation

2) Candidate evaluation workflow
   - Bake candidate image with new driver (e.g., 550).
   - Deploy to a small canary pool (single AZ if possible).
   - Run validations + perf canary with tighter observability:
     - capture per-attempt duration
     - log bundle pointers
     - tag by image_channel=candidate, gpu_type, region

3) Rollback trigger (automatic or operator-driven)
   - If nccl_smoke failure rate spikes > 0.5% over 1h (candidate) OR if we see any hang cluster, pause promotions and roll back.

Pinning decisions (tentative)
- For the sprint, pin CUDA userspace at 12.2 for “stable” until the EFA/NCCL hang is resolved.
- Driver 535 line is the current stable baseline for A100.
- Revisit after staged rollout data: if we can get driver 550 stable on A100 without increased flakes, we can move stable.

Open questions
- Should we validate with the exact same container image used by serving runtime (preferred), or keep a dedicated validation image that only checks NCCL + minimal CUDA? (Risk: divergence.)
- Do we need a separate H100 baseline and thresholds (likely yes). Who owns the baseline numbers? (Nina + Aisha?)
- How do we gate on EFA readiness explicitly? Do we have a reliable preflight command/metric that indicates EFA is healthy enough to run NCCL?

Notes from testing sessions
- 2025-10-02: bake failed due to CUDA minor mismatch. Root cause: base AMI pulled a newer nvidia-container-toolkit that assumed newer driver features. Proposed: lock apt repo versions for nvidia-container-toolkit during image bake.
- 2025-10-07: saw nccl_smoke flakes when validation started immediately after kubelet join. Added “initial delay” experiment (60s) reduced flakes in ad-hoc test.
- 2025-10-12: metric tag explosion incident briefly masked true failure rate; after cardinality fix, nccl_smoke failure rate for candidate lane was worse than initially believed.

Commands / snippets (for reproducibility)
- Host driver check:
  - nvidia-smi
  - modinfo nvidia | grep version
- CUDA userspace check (inside validation container):
  - nvcc --version (if present) / nvidia-smi reports driver only, not toolkit
  - python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda)" (only if torch-based test image)
- NCCL test (example):
  - all_reduce_perf -b 8M -e 256M -f 2 -g 8 (adjust per GPU count)
  - Set timeout in wrapper to avoid infinite hangs

Failure triage pointers (when you hit a bad combo)
- If GPU health check fails (Xid/ECC): quarantine immediately; don’t keep retrying NCCL.
- If driver parity fails: almost always an image drift issue; reimage (don’t quarantine unless repeats).
- If NCCL hangs:
  - try one reboot and one reimage
  - if repeats on same host: quarantine and file infra ticket with instance details

Appendix: mapping to provisioning readiness gates
- driver/CUDA parity gate should assert:
  - host driver version matches expected image channel (stable/candidate)
  - validation container CUDA userspace matches expected lane
- nccl_smoke gate should record:
  - duration, retries, and a log bundle pointer
  - pass/fail plus “timeout vs explicit error” classification

TODO (next edits)

- Fill in exact EFA driver/libfabric versions from the latest p4d bake.
- Decide: do we want to support mixed GPU SKU pools? If yes, matrix expands and we need stricter pinning.
